## Story Goal

The queue row in `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` shows, at a glance, that a ticket has a recorded breach — a first-response breach and a resolution breach drawn as **two visibly different marks** (their own surface and edge, not only a caption), each with a caption from the resource files, each with the breach time formatted through `useFormatters` (BR-3), each in both languages (BR-6). Nothing on the screen decides what "late" means: the row draws only the `breaches` array the API sent — no clock, no `new Date()`, no comparison with `Date.now()`.

**Out of scope** (owned elsewhere; do not touch here):

- Any change under `api/` — that is **SERVICE-LEVELS-3-API (CRM-110)**.
- Filtering or sorting the queue by lateness — **TICKETS-2-WEB** owns queue filters and no story asks for this one.
- A dashboard or a count of breaches — the reports feature, not this sprint.
- Changing escalation or priority-raise behaviour — **SERVICE-LEVELS-4-\***.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the row shows only `subject`, `status`, `priority`, assignee name, `createdAt` (TicketQueuePage.tsx:143–155). Nothing tells an agent that a ticket has a recorded breach.
- **New behaviour:** if `ticket.breaches` is non-empty, each entry renders as a distinct visual mark on the row **with its own caption** (`ticketQueue.breachFirstResponse` / `ticketQueue.breachResolution`) and the breach time formatted through `useFormatters().formatDate(breachedAt)`. Both kinds may be present; both are shown. A ticket with no breaches renders exactly as today.
- **S-5:** the row must not compute lateness. No `new Date()`, no `Date.now()`, no comparison of `createdAt` with anything. The `breaches` array **is** the answer.

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts`

Add a `Breach` type and a `breaches` field to `Ticket`. Place the type immediately above `Ticket` (near lines 17–19) with a short comment about S-5. Keep the field required (the API always sends it, empty array when none) — mirror the way `allowedTransitions: string[]` is required at line 42.

### 4 — Render the breach marks on the row

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

Import the new label and, at the top of the file:

- Line 17 — extend the import: `import { breachLabel, priorityLabel, statusLabel } from './ticket-labels';`
- No new hook needed; the `formatDate` the `Row` already receives (parameter at line 60, used at line 153) is the same formatter you use for `breachedAt`.

Immediately **after** the muted meta line (end of `</Text>` at line 155) and **before** the assignee `<Stack direction="row" gap={2}>` at line 157, insert a breach strip. It renders nothing when `ticket.breaches` is empty:

```tsx
{ticket.breaches.length > 0 ? (
  <Stack direction="row" gap={1} as="ul" className="ticket-row__breaches">
    {ticket.breaches.map((breach) => (
      <li
        key={breach.kind}
        className={`ticket-row__breach ticket-row__breach--${breach.kind}`}
      >
        <span className="ticket-row__breach-tag">
          {breachLabel(t, breach.kind)}
        </span>
        <span className="ticket-row__breach-when">
          {t.ticketQueue.breachAt.replace('{when}', formatDate(breach.breachedAt))}
        </span>
      </li>
    ))}
  </Stack>
) : null}
```

Notes:

- **Each kind is its own `<li>` with its own modifier class** (`--first_response` / `--resolution`), because the intake requires two different promises to be told apart the way notes and replies are — the surface and edge are the glance, the caption is the answer.
- **Caption always renders**, even though the surface and edge already signal the breach: this is the same rule `TicketThread.css:32–34` names (screen-reader users and colour-blind users need the word).
- Use the row's existing `formatDate` (BR-3). Do **not** call `Date`, `Intl`, `toLocaleString`, or `toISOString`.
- If your `Stack` primitive does not accept `as`, use a plain `<ul className="ticket-row__breaches">` with `Stack`-style spacing on the `<ul>` in CSS; confirm by reading `web/src/shared/ui/Stack.tsx` before you change the JSX.

### 5 — Style the two marks (surface + edge, logical properties only)

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.css` (if it does not exist — check first with `list_dir web/src/pages/tickets`). Otherwise append to the existing sibling stylesheet the page already imports.

Import the CSS from `TicketQueuePage.tsx` (near line 1, next to the other imports).

Model the two marks on `TicketThread.css` — a padded strip with a coloured inline-start edge, inset from the row's content, one modifier per kind. **Logical properties only**; `no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` fails on `left`/`right`/`padding-left`/`margin-right`/`[dir=]`.

```css
/* A breach on the row is drawn the way a note is drawn on the thread: its
   own surface and edge, not only a caption, so a scanner sees a different
   block before reading a word (S-5's stored fact, made visible). Logical
   properties throughout so the mark sits on the correct side in Arabic
   without a second rule (LANGUAGES-2-WEB / no-mirrored-styles.test.ts). */
.ticket-row__breaches {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}

.ticket-row__breach {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--space-1);
  padding-inline: var(--space-2);
  padding-block: var(--space-1);
  border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--color-danger);
  background: var(--color-bg-surface);
}

.ticket-row__breach--first_response {
  border-inline-start-color: var(--color-warning);
}

.ticket-row__breach--resolution {
  border-inline-start-color: var(--color-danger);
}

.ticket-row__breach-tag {
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--color-text-strong);
}

.ticket-row__breach-when {
  color: var(--color-text-muted);
}
```

If `--color-warning` or `--color-strong` is not in `web/src/shared/ui/tokens.css`, use `--color-text` / `--color-danger` / `--color-border-strong` — grep `tokens.css` before naming a variable.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty `breaches` array** — most rows. Render nothing between the meta line and the assignee stack. Enforced at TicketQueuePage.tsx (the `ticket.breaches.length > 0 ?` guard added in Task 4). Test in Task 7.1.
- **Both a first-response and a resolution breach on the same ticket** — the intake calls this out explicitly. Both `<li>` render, in the order the API sent them (kind ascending: `first_response`, `resolution` — the API repo query orders by `kind`, see `api/src/features/service-levels/service-levels.repository.js:73`). Test in Task 7.3.
- **Unknown `kind` from a newer API** — `breachLabel` falls back to the raw kind (`?? kind`), matching the precedent in `ticket-labels.ts:22`. The CSS modifier `--<kind>` simply matches nothing and the base `.ticket-row__breach` styling still applies. **Do not throw.**
- **RTL (Arabic)** — the mark sits on the row's start edge in both directions because every property is `-inline-*`. Verified by `web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`.
- **A ticket the API returns with a breach whose `breachedAt` is a plain ISO string** — passed straight into `formatDate`, which is what already handles `createdAt` (TicketQueuePage.tsx:153). No parsing on the screen.
- **A test fixture missing `breaches`** — TypeScript refuses to compile (`breaches` is required on `Ticket`). Run `cd web && npm run build` after edits — this is the only step that typechecks; `npm test` (vitest) does not.
- **API old enough not to send `breaches`** — the field is required in the type. Unlike `allowedTransitions` (which was defensively `?? []` at TicketQueuePage.tsx:120 for exactly this concern), SERVICE-LEVELS-3-API is a hard prerequisite for this WEB story and ships in the same sprint. Do **not** add a defensive default; a runtime crash surfaces a broken deploy, which is what we want. (If you disagree, raise it before implementing — do not silently default.)

## Done Criteria

- [x] A ticket with a recorded breach says so on its row, before the controls that act on it.
- [x] The two kinds are drawn differently — different class AND different rule — with a caption each.
- [x] A ticket with no breach claims none, and the screen computes no deadline of its own.
- [x] The time it was missed is in the reader's locale (BR-3), never the raw stamp.
- [x] A ticket from an API that sends no `breaches` renders rather than blanking the queue.
- [x] Both languages (BR-6). `cd web && npm test` (343) and `npm run build` pass; `cd api && npm test` (563) untouched.
- [x] No `api/` file changed. No commit, doc or ignore-file entry mentions AI assistance.

**A mutation passed because jsdom applies no stylesheets.** Making both edges
identical — the whole "visibly different, not only a caption" criterion —
failed nothing: a component test can see class names and not the rules behind
them. The fix was already in this codebase: `no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` reads
CSS as text, so this test does too, and asserts the two modifier rules say
something different. Which difference is a design decision that may change;
that there IS one is the criterion.
